feedback.title: Below target, and East's known void backs the trump
feedback.summary: You need this trick. East acts after you and is already known void in Spades, so East cannot overtrump you no matter what East holds — this trump is as close to certain as the evidence here allows.
points: Decisive: the earlier trick shows East discarding a Diamond when Spades were led, so East holds no more Spades this hand and cannot beat any trump you play.
Supporting: you are below target and still need this trick, which is why taking it deliberately — rather than risking a pass — matters here.
You hold no Hearts, so trumping is legal. Nothing else on the table beats a trump, and the only seat left to act cannot supply one.

feedback.title: Giving up a trick the known void makes safe to try
feedback.summary: The two of Clubs is off-suit and non-trump; it cannot win this trick under any circumstance, and discarding it gives up a trick that East's confirmed void makes unusually safe to attempt.
points: You are below target and still need this trick; passing on it does not reduce what is still needed later.
East's void is specifically in Spades (this trick's trump), not a suit unrelated to the decision — it directly removes the usual risk of being overtrumped.
This is not a cautious, defensible choice: the evidence here specifically supports trying, not holding back.

author_notes: EC-055 checkpoint-3 coverage: first Mixed tactical reading scenario, combining two already-supported signals rather than inventing a new capability. Decisive signal: East's known void in trump (Spades), derived from the observed trick exactly as in play_void_tracking_001/005 — this is what elevates the trump play from merely probable (as in play_safe_probable_003/004, where the responding seat's holding is unresolved) to effectively certain, since a void seat cannot supply the one card type that could beat a trump. Supporting signal: South is below target and needs this trick, which motivates why taking it deliberately is the reviewed choice rather than a neutral or cautious one. Neither signal alone fully explains the rating: the void alone does not say South should try for the trick, and the below-target state alone does not say the attempt is nearly certain to succeed.
